cases.promptMarkdown:

93/42/EEC. We're still selling it. How long can we keep placing it on the EU market
before we have to be fully MDR certified?

## Class III implantable device, MDD (93/42/EEC) certificate

**Class:** III (implantable — but class III alone sets the date; the implantable distinction only matters for IIb)
**Route:** 120(3a) — certificate issued under Directive 93/42/EEC
**Deadline:** **31 December 2027** — conditional on 120(3c)

| Question | Answer | Basis |
|---|---|---|
| Which paragraph applies | Article 120(3a)(a) — device holds a notified-body certificate under 93/42/EEC, valid by virtue of Article 120(2) | `[verified]` |
| Class-dependent date | 31 December 2027, for all class III devices (and class IIb implantables other than the listed exceptions) | `[verified]` |
| 3c conditions met? | **Not established — you need to confirm this.** All five are cumulative | `[verified]` (provision), your facts |

So: from today, roughly 15½ months of placing on the market, then MDR certification is required — **but only if you qualified for the extension in the first place.**

### The conditional half

The 2027 date is not automatic. Article 120(3c) requires **all five** of:

- (a) continued compliance with 93/42/EEC;
- (b) **no significant changes** in design and intended purpose;
- (c) no unacceptable risk to health or safety;
- (d) a **quality management system** per Article 10(9) in place **no later than 26 May 2024**;
- (e) a **formal application** lodged with a notified body (Annex VII, 4.3 first subpara) **no later than 26 May 2024**, and a **signed written agreement** with that notified body **no later than 26 September 2024**.

Note what happened to 26 May 2024: it is no longer the market deadline — that was the original 2017 text, now superseded by Regulation (EU) 2023/607. It is now the date the QMS and the application were due. Those deadlines have passed. If either was missed, the extension was never available to you and your position is different from the one above.

**What would change this:** any of the 3c conditions not having been met — most commonly a missed 26 May 2024 application or QMS date, or a design/intended-purpose change since certification that counts as "significant." Also worth confirming your MDD certificate's status under Article 120(2), which this reference does not cover.

One thing that applies right now regardless: under **120(3d)**, MDR's requirements on post-market surveillance, market surveillance, vigilance, and registration of economic operators and devices apply to your device **in place of** the corresponding MDD requirements, throughout the transition. `[verified]`

If the question of whether a change you've made is "significant" under 3c(b) is live for you, that turns on MDCG guidance, which I don't have in front of me — I'd rather flag it than produce a view from memory.

## Limits

> This covers MDR Article 120(3) and (3a)–(3d) as amended by Regulation (EU) 2023/607, retrieved verbatim from the Official Journal on 2026-09-10. It does **not** cover Article 120's other paragraphs, **IVDR Article 110** (the parallel IVD transition, whose dates differ), MDCG guidance including on what counts as a significant change, Annex VII, or national practice. The transition is conditional and fact-specific; this is a first-pass aid, not legal or regulatory advice, and not a substitute for your notified body or a qualified regulatory professional.

## Short answer

**31 December 2027** — but only if you met two hard gates that already passed in 2024. If you missed them, your extension never applied and you should not be placing product on the market today.

## The rule

Regulation (EU) 2023/607 rewrote Article 120 of the MDR. Your MDD certificate is deemed valid beyond its printed expiry date, until:

| Device class | Deadline to stop *placing on the market* |
|---|---|
| **Class III, and Class IIb implantable** (except the "WET" list — sutures, staples, dental fillings/braces/crowns, screws, wedges, plates, wires, pins, clips, connectors) | **31 Dec 2027** |
| Other Class IIb, Class IIa, Class I sterile/measuring, and the WET list | 31 Dec 2028 |

So for a Class III implantable: **31 December 2027**. That's roughly 15½ months from today. On 1 January 2028 you need an MDR certificate in hand to keep placing units on the market.

## The conditions — check these first

The extension is conditional (Art. 120(3c)). The two that bite:

- **26 May 2024** — QMS compliant with Art. 10(9) MDR in place, *and* a formal MDR conformity-assessment application lodged with a notified body.
- **26 September 2024** — written agreement signed between you and that notified body.

Plus the ongoing ones: continued MDD compliance, no significant change in design or intended purpose, and no unacceptable risk.

Both deadlines are in the past. If you didn't lodge and sign in time, there is no extension, no grace mechanism, and no retroactive fix — your MDD certificate stopped covering new placement on the market at that point. That's the first thing to confirm, ahead of planning anything for 2027.

## Three things people commonly get wrong here

**"Placing on the market" ≠ "selling."** The 2027 date stops *first* placement of each individual unit on the EU market. Units already lawfully placed can continue to be made available and put into service with **no sell-off deadline** — 2023/607 deleted it. Stock already downstream on 31 Dec 2027 is not stranded.

**Your MDD notified body isn't doing surveillance anymore.** Since 26 May 2024, surveillance of the legacy device sits with the MDR notified body under that written agreement (Art. 120(3e)). If your MDD body has exited the market, that transfer needs to have happened.

**No significant change.** Any change to design or intended purpose during the transition voids the extension for that device. Worth a hard look if you've made any modifications since 2021.

## If your device is custom-made

Class III custom-made implantables had a separate, earlier deadline: **26 May 2026**. That has already passed. If any part of your portfolio is custom-made, it needed an MDR certificate before that date.

## Practically

Notified body capacity for Class III implantables is the binding constraint, not the legal date. Fifteen months is thin for a Class III review cycle if you're not already deep in review with clinical evaluation closed out. I'd want to know where your application actually sits — and whether there's a realistic issuance date from your NB, not just a queue position.

One thing to watch: the Commission has signalled a targeted MDR/IVDR reform package. I don't know whether anything was tabled or adopted between May and September 2026 that touches these dates. Worth checking the current consolidated Article 120 and any 2026 amending regulation — I can do that if you enable web access.

## Bottom line

**31 December 2027** — that's the last date you can *place the device on the EU market* under the legacy MDD certificate. It is not automatic; it's conditional, and the qualifying conditions all had deadlines that are now in the past.

## Where the date comes from

Article 120 MDR, as amended by Regulation (EU) 2023/607 (in force 20 March 2023). The amendment replaced the old flat 26 May 2024 cliff with risk-tiered dates:

| Device class | Legacy placing-on-market deadline |
|---|---|
| Class III and Class IIb implantable (excl. the "well-established technology" list — sutures, staples, dental fillings/braces/crowns, screws, wedges, plates, wires, pins, clips, connectors) | **31 Dec 2027** |
| Other Class IIb, Class IIa, Class I sterile/measuring/reusable-surgical | 31 Dec 2028 |
| Class III custom-made implantables | 26 May 2026 (already passed) |

A standard Class III implantable lands in the first row. One thing to check: if your device is on that well-established-technology exclusion list, you're in the 2028 bucket instead — but that list is mostly Class IIb items, so it's unlikely to change your answer.

Note the extension applies **even past the printed expiry date on your MDD certificate**. A certificate that expired in, say, 2024 is deemed valid to 31 Dec 2027 provided the conditions below were met.

## The conditions — verify you actually met these

Article 120(3c). All five must hold, and the two hard deadlines are behind you:

1. Device continues to comply with the MDD.
2. **No significant change** in design or intended purpose since the certificate was issued. (MDCG 2020-3 rev.1 is the interpretive guidance; this is the condition most often tripped by incremental changes.)
3. No unacceptable risk to health or safety.
4. **By 26 May 2024** — MDR-compliant QMS in place (Art. 10(9)).
5. **By 26 May 2024** — formal MDR conformity-assessment application lodged with a notified body, **and by 26 September 2024** a signed written agreement with that notified body.

If #4 or #5 was missed, the extension never attached to your device and the legal basis for placing it on the market lapsed at that point — not something that can be cured retroactively. Worth confirming you have the dated application acknowledgement and the countersigned NB agreement on file, because that's the evidence a competent authority will ask for.

## Two things people get wrong

**"Placing on the market" ≠ "selling through."** The deadline bites on first making each individual unit available in the Union. Regulation 2023/607 **deleted the sell-off deadline entirely** (old Art. 120(4)). So units you've already placed on the market before 31 Dec 2027 can continue to be distributed, made available and put into service with **no end date** — subject to shelf life. This materially changes end-of-transition inventory planning: you can build stock and place it before the cliff.

**MDR obligations already apply to you now.** Since 26 May 2021, legacy devices under the transition are subject to MDR rules on post-market surveillance, vigilance, market surveillance, registration of economic operators and device registration — only the pre-market conformity-assessment requirements stay under MDD. Also relevant: the Art. 10a supply-interruption notification duty (6 months' advance notice where discontinuation could cause serious harm), applicable since 10 January 2025 via Regulation (EU) 2024/1860, and phased mandatory EUDAMED module use on the same instrument.

Surveillance of the legacy certificate: once the written agreement was signed, your MDR notified body assumes the appropriate surveillance; the original MDD NB is otherwise still on the hook (Art. 120(3e)).

## What I can't confirm from here

The Commission had a targeted MDR reform package in preparation through 2025–2026, and further date relief was openly discussed given notified body capacity. Nothing amending the 2027/2028 dates had been *adopted* as of my knowledge cutoff. Since we're now 15 months from the deadline, that's exactly the window where a change would land — so check the consolidated Article 120 on EUR-Lex and the MDCG page before you set internal plans. If you enable web access I'll pull the current text.

Practically: with ~15 months left and NB review queues for Class III implantables typically running well over a year, the live question is less "how long do I have" and more "where is my MDR application in my notified body's queue right now."

Note the carve-out: sutures, staples, dental fillings, braces, crowns, screws, wedges, plates, wires, pins, clips and connectors are treated as Class IIb-other and get 2028 instead. A Class III implantable almost certainly does not fall in that list.

## The conditions — check these before you rely on 2027

1. The device **continues to comply with the MDD**.
2. **No significant changes** in design or intended purpose since the certificate was issued.
3. The device presents **no unacceptable risk** to health or safety.
4. **By 26 May 2024** you had an MDR Article 10(9)-compliant **QMS** in place.
5. **By 26 May 2024** you (or your EU authorised rep) had **lodged a formal MDR application** with a notified body for that device or its intended substitute.
6. **By 26 September 2024** you and the notified body had **signed a written agreement**.

Conditions 4–6 are the ones that bite. They are not curable retroactively. If you did not file by May 2024 and sign by September 2024, the extension never attached to your device and you have been placing a non-conforming device on the market since then. If that is your situation, stop and talk to your competent authority about an Article 59 derogation — that is the only route left.

Also note: MDR post-market surveillance, vigilance, registration and market-surveillance obligations **already apply** to your legacy device (Article 120(3)). Only the pre-market conformity assessment sits under the MDD.

**"Placing on the market" is per unit, not per product line.** Each individual device must be first made available in the EU on or before 31 Dec 2027. Manufacturing date doesn't matter; first transfer into the EU supply chain does.

**There is no sell-off deadline anymore.** Regulation 2023/607 deleted the old 26 May 2025 sell-off provision. Devices lawfully placed on the market under the transitional regime may continue to be **made available and put into service indefinitely** by distributors and hospitals. So stock in the channel on 1 Jan 2028 is still sellable — you just can't add more to the channel.

## Practical timing

For a Class III implantable, a first-time MDR review with clinical evaluation, and likely a PMCF plan plus the Article 54 clinical evaluation consultation procedure (expert panel scrutiny, which adds real calendar time), notified bodies are quoting long queues. Working back from 31 Dec 2027 with ~15 months to go, your technical documentation should already be submitted and in review. If it isn't, treat this as the critical path and get a dated milestone plan from your notified body in writing.

The Commission signalled in 2025 that it would bring forward a **targeted revision of the medical devices framework**, with a proposal expected around end-2026. Industry has pushed for further relief on the 2027/2028 dates. As of my knowledge through May 2026 **nothing had changed in law** — 31 Dec 2027 stands. Given today is September 2026, please confirm current status with your notified body or the MDCG guidance page before making a plan that depends on any extension. Do not plan around a hoped-for extension; plan around 2027.

One thing I can't tell from your question: whether your device is custom-made. Class III custom-made implantables had a separate deadline of 26 May 2026, which has now passed. If that's your situation, tell me and the answer is different.

I'm giving you the regulatory structure here, not legal advice — for a Class III implantable this should be confirmed with your regulatory counsel and notified body.
